definition.query: what is AI agent access control
definition.content: AI agent access control is the enforcement layer that determines what resources an autonomous agent can read, write, connect to, and execute — at the architectural level, not the policy-document level. Unlike traditional RBAC for human users, AI agent access control must account for emergent autonomy: an agent given a high-level goal can pursue it in unexpected ways, making ambient authority (full host access) a structural failure rather than a configuration error.

faq.q: What is capability-based security for AI agents?
faq.a: Capability-based security (OCap) is a model where an agent cannot perform any action unless it holds a cryptographic reference — a capability — to an object that can perform that action. There is no global filesystem, no global network, and no ambient process authority. Every permission is explicit, attenuable, non-forgeable, and revocable. AgentForge implements OCap as its core security primitive.

faq.q: Why is full host access a security failure for agent frameworks?
faq.a: Full host access means the agent can do anything the user account can do — read any file, send any network request, execute any program, access any API key in the environment. A single malicious skill, a single CVE, or a single prompt injection payload gains the full blast radius of the user who installed the agent. The 2026 Claw Chain disclosure (CVE-2026-44112, CVSS 9.6) demonstrated this concretely: a single foothold in OpenClaw escalated to credential theft and persistent backdoor placement.

faq.q: How does AgentForge's WASM sandbox work?
faq.a: AgentForge skills run as WebAssembly modules inside a WASM runtime with explicitly granted capabilities. Every skill is verified by SHA-256 hash before execution. A skill cannot request additional permissions at runtime — it receives them at spawn time, and the runtime enforces the restriction at the instruction level. A weather checker skill cannot escalate to filesystem access or arbitrary network connections.

faq.q: What is the OWASP ASI Top 10?
faq.a: The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (ASI) is a peer-reviewed risk taxonomy published in 2026 that identifies the most critical security risks facing autonomous AI agents. Unlike the OWASP LLM Top 10 (which secures what AI says), the ASI Top 10 secures what AI does. It covers risks including Agent Goal Hijack (ASI01), Tool Misuse (ASI02), Supply Chain Compromise (ASI04), Insecure Inter-Agent Communication (ASI07), and Rogue Agents (ASI10).

faq.q: How does AgentForge compare to OpenClaw on security?
faq.a: OpenClaw runs as a Node.js application with full host privileges by default and an npm dependency tree that Cisco classified as a 'threat multiplier.' AgentForge compiles to a 6 MB static Go binary with no runtime dependencies, no Node.js, no Python venv, and no Tauri webview. AgentForge's OCap model means every agent spawns with zero permissions; OpenClaw's model means every agent inherits the user's full authority by default.
